title: Consolidated MVP: Reduce Dashboard Cards, Trace Depth, and Cost Breakdown Granularity
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Trim and re-scope the Redwood Console observability surface for an MVP launch. The goal is to reduce engineering and design effort by narrowing dashboards to 4 high-value cards, limiting trace UI depth to single-request sampling with 10s retention in the UI, and collapsing cost breakdown into per-route aggregates only. This PRD clarifies what is deferred versus what must land for the MVP so the launch target remains achievable without compromising SLO observability for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: 4 cards implemented (Route-level latency P50/P95, Request rate, Error rate, Cost per 1k tokens) and each card supports timespan selection (15m/1h/24h)
Tracing: UI shows traces for sampled requests with single-span waterfall and up to 10s of event timeline; deep trace drilldowns and span-level flame graphs are deferred
Cost breakdown: Console exposes per-route cost aggregation and a top-10 routes list; per-token waterfall and per-model micro-breakdowns are deferred
Rollout flags: All new UI components behind feature flag 'obs_mvp_trim' and gating is testable in staging
Performance: Dashboard renders within 800ms for orgs with <10k requests/day in staging dataset
QA: E2E test covering dashboard card load, trace sampling view, and route cost aggregation exists and passes on CI
decisions: Defer per-token and per-model cost waterfall to post-MVP to save ~4 sprint-weeks of backend work
Limit trace depth to surface a lightweight sampled trace view; advanced trace exploration will be a separate initiative
Standardize card set to 4 core metrics to reduce design/engineering iteration and improve clarity for early users
tradeoffs: Reduced granularity in cost visibility may frustrate power users; mitigated by clear messaging and a product plan for advanced cost features
Shallow trace views decrease time-to-implementation but reduce ability to debug complex latency issues; will be compensated with improved logging links and request IDs
Smaller dashboard surface reduces initial telemetry noise but may hide regressions that would have been captured by deeper metrics; acceptance criteria include targeted E2E checks to mitigate
